prize_parts.citation: For the development of general palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling
For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand breaks

statement.case_for: I keep my round-1 configuration after reading the full exchange and the chair's questions. B052 is the most broadly supported and best-attributed candidate: four members include it, every one of them credits exactly Buchwald and Hartwig, and no one argues for Kosugi. Kosugi's tin-amide reaction was a real precursor but not general or ligand-controlled, so a citation worded around general catalysis answers the priority question. Ligand design and mechanism turned a narrow reaction into a routine one used daily in medicinal chemistry and materials synthesis, and the 2010 prize left C-N bonds out. B004 adds the second thing I test for, a discovery that changed what researchers and clinicians can do: deaminase chemistry on a single nucleotide, with the adenine editor needing directed evolution of an enzyme with no natural DNA substrate, reproduced in many laboratories and now in patients. Reading Chabes's case, the avoidance of break-driven repair is a distinct chemical advantage over the 2020 Cas9 platform, not just a re-targeting of it. The two parts come from different corners of chemistry and together use exactly three names.
statement.case_against: The strongest weakness is the B004 credit. Naming Liu alone leaves out Komor and Gaudelli, who led the cytosine and adenine editors, and Kondo and Nishida's Target-AID work was independent, so the credit can look like honouring the laboratory head. Base editing also follows the 2020 prize closely and long-term safety and clinical outcome data are still emerging, so it may be judged earlier than B052. A two-part prize also gives B052 less weight than the three members who want it as the whole prize. For B052, the sequel-to-2010 objection is real, and Hartwig's presence on the C-H functionalisation entry means the same people could be recognised under another ID.

responses.point: Andrei proposes B004 as the whole prize for Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, arguing that avoiding break-driven repair makes it a well-defined chemical reaction for biologists, and flags Target-AID and the closeness to the 2020 prize.
responses.response: I agree with your chemical argument and it is why B004 stays in my configuration. I do not move to your single-part prize, because I think B004 alone is less ready than B052: the clinical outcome record is thin and the Komor, Gaudelli and Kondo, Nishida attribution is open. The three-name cap forces a choice. I would rather credit the person who conceived both editor classes and let the citation describe the method than drop Komor or Gaudelli arbitrarily. If the committee insists on crediting all inventors, I would then prefer your single-part B004 to a B052 plus B004 pairing that names someone I cannot justify excluding.

responses.point: Xiaodong says Kosugi's reaction was not general or ligand-controlled and that B052 has the broadest cross-subfield support and a clean two-laureate citation, while admitting his 1994-1995 timeline rests on recollection.
responses.response: Your point on generality is the answer I will use for the chair's Kosugi question, since the files do not settle the dates and I cannot either. Even if Kosugi's priority were close, the contribution that made C-N coupling usable was the ligand-controlled catalyst and the mechanism, which is what Buchwald and Hartwig built, so the word general in the citation does the work. I would not stretch your claim into 'free of precedent'. I differ only on completeness: a two-name B052 uses just two of three seats, and I think the third is better spent on a biomolecular tool.

responses.point: Heiner proposes B002 with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen as a single physical-chemical principle, and notes the overexpression and Pappu and Mittag credit problems himself.
responses.response: Your own reservations are the reason I keep B002 as an alternative. The 2009 P-granule and 2012 multivalency work are real foundations, but the physiological relevance of many condensates is still disputed, and a three-name cap omits Pappu and Mittag, whose sequence-grammar framework is part of the chemistry. I also do not see a reason to choose it over B004 on maturity, because it is fifteen years old but carries the disputed in vivo claims. Whether it is Chemistry or Physiology or Medicine is a further open question that I cannot settle. I would support B002 in a later year if the relevance debate narrows.

responses.point: Peter makes B052 the whole prize, based on ligand design and the most-used C-N method in process chemistry, and treats Kosugi as a real precursor whose omission invites a priority argument.
responses.response: I accept your argument and treat B052 as the anchor. I answer your concern by wording the citation around the general, ligand-controlled method. Where I differ is whether it should stand alone. Your point that it is a mature method does not tell me it needs no companion, and I think a second part lets the prize reach biomedicine. I also note you listed B037 as an alternative, and I agree it is the strongest fallback.

responses.point: Peter proposes B009 for Gray and Winkler, with clean two-person attribution and four decades of confirmation, and admits it is close to his field and rests on Marcus theory.
responses.response: The attribution is clean and I take the maturity argument, but your own caveats weigh on me: the Marcus overlap, the Hopfield and the Dutton and Moser priority questions, and the fact that no other member ranks it in the top eight. Its reach into biomedicine and materials is also narrower than the two parts I support. I would reconsider only if a second member outside the field supported it.

uncertainties: Whether Liu alone is an acceptable credit for base editing, or whether the committee requires Komor and Gaudelli, which would push toward a single-part B004 or a different pairing.
How the committee weighs Kosugi's precursor work in C-N coupling, which I cannot verify from the files.
Whether base editing is distinct enough from the 2020 CRISPR prize and mature enough given the emerging clinical data.
Whether a two-part prize splitting three seats will command a majority when three members prefer B052 alone.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. My Linkoping biosensor and peptide work and my postdoc mentors Stevens and Boey have no connection to the credited names on B052, B004 or the listed alternatives, so no recusal is needed.
